text: Chronic unpredictable stress altered the anxiety-like response to the cannabinoid CB(1) receptor agonist HU-210 [3-(1,1-dimethylheptyl)-(-)-11-hydroxy-delta 8-tetrahydrocannabinol] in the elevated plus maze. Male Long-Evans rats were unstressed or exposed to a 21-day chronic unpredictable stress regimen, then divided into vehicle, 10, and 50 microg/kg HU-210 groups. In unstressed animals, the low dose produced an anxiolytic response and the high dose an anxiogenic response. In stressed animals, both low and high doses induced anxiogenic responses. These findings suggest chronic stress enhances cannabinoid receptor responsivity or interacting systems implicated in emotional states.
